summary: Emilio Teza was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Padua and under Anton Boller at the University of Vienna. He held professorships at the universities of Bologna (1860–1866), Pisa (1866–1889), and Padua (1889–1912).

Emily T. Yeh is a Tibetology scholar who studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology and the University of California, Berkeley. She joined the faculty at the University of Colorado Boulder around 2003.

Emma Georgina Rothschild is a historian who studied at Somerville College and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. She served as a professor at the University of Cambridge from circa 1988 to 2008 and joined Harvard University around 2008.

Emma J. Flatt is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. She was an assistant professor at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (2012–2021) before becoming an associate professor at Nanyang Technological University in 2023.

Emma Salter works in religious studies and Indology, having studied at the University of Glamorgan, Cardiff University, and the University of Huddersfield. She has held posts at the Open University, Greenhead College, and the International Baccalaureate.

Emmanuel Forchhammer, a scholar of Indology, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, studied at the University of Leipzig under Hermann Brockhaus, Georg von der Gabelentz, and Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer. He served at the University of Rangoon and British Burma's government.
Emmanuel Lang was an Indology scholar who studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales, where he studied under Sylvain Lévi.

Emmie te Nijenhuis is an Indologist who studied at Utrecht Conservatory, Utrecht School of the Arts, and Utrecht University, completing her PhD under Jan Gonda. She served as associate professor of Indian musicology at Utrecht University (1964–1988).

Emmy Wellesz was a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She completed her Ph.D. at the University of Vienna between 1907 and 1921 under doctoral supervisor Josef Strzygowski.

Enamul Haque was a historian and Indologist who studied at the University of Dhaka and the University of Oxford. He served as Director General of the Bangladesh National Museum and president of the International Centre for Study of Bengal Art.

Encho Tamura was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and Japanology. He studied at Kyushu and Kyoto universities, held multiple posts at Kyushu University from 1941 to 1980, and was a professor at Kumamoto University from circa 1978 to 1982.

Endo Asai was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and Rissho University. He served on the faculty at Minobusan University, where he later became president, and as a professor at Rissho University.

Eng Jin Ooi is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Mahidol University supervised by Giuliano Giustarini. He lectured at Mahidol University (2022–2024) and became lecturer and dean at the International Buddhist College in 2025.

Enga Teramoto was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Kumbum Monastery in 1903. He later taught as a lecturer at Kyoto University (circa 1908–1926) and as a professor at Otani University from 1915.

Enichi Ocho was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Daijō Tokiwa at the University of Tokyo. He worked as a researcher at the Academy of Oriental Culture from 1931 and served as professor at Otani University from 1949 to 1976.

Enno Littmann was a linguist and historian who studied at Berlin, Greifswald, and Halle-Wittenberg. He taught at Princeton and held professorships at the universities of Strasbourg (from 1906), Göttingen (1913–1917), Bonn (1918–1921), and Tübingen (1921–1951).

Enrico Pappacena was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied under Michele Kerbaker at the University of Naples Federico II. He served as a professor incaricato at the University of Bari from 1946 to 1960.

Enrique Soms y Castelín was an Indologist and linguist. He served as Professor of Greek at the University of Salamanca from circa 1888 to 1913 and at the Complutense University of Madrid from 1891 to 1913.

Enryo Inoue was a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Ernest Fenollosa and Tanzan Hara at the University of Tokyo. He founded Toyo University, serving as lecturer and manager there from circa 1887 to 1905.

Ensho Kanakura was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied at the University of Tokyo. He served as a professor at Tohoku University (1926–1960), Rissho University (circa 1957–1978), and as president of Miyagi University of Education (1967).
